title: President Oaks Calls for Constitutional Compromise and Peace at National Cathedral
text:
Speaking on the eve of Constitution Day, President Dallin H. Oaks of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints delivered a speech at the Washington National Cathedral urging unity and compromise to preserve religious freedom. He highlighted the U.S. Constitution as a model for self-government and discussed the church's history in seeking freedom through peaceful negotiation.
President Dallin H. Oaks, President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, spoke at the Washington National Cathedral on Wednesday, emphasizing the U.S. Constitution's role in self-government and religious freedom.
He highlighted the church's history as refugees and its commitment to peacemaking and compromise. Oaks outlined key constitutional principles: popular sovereignty, separation of powers, individual rights, and rule of law, urging loyalty to the system over individuals. He called for understanding and fairness in resolving conflicts, stressing the importance of upholding essential rights for all
